proposals.announcement_evidence: to maintain, enhance, and demonstrate advanced microcircuit emulation technology capability and to continue with basic technology and production development
proposals.lexicon_quote: tteries (Battery Network), Additive Manufacturing (AM), and Advanced Microcircuit Emulation (AME). -The 3D Technical Data Modernization / Model Based Enter
proposals.rationale: The announcement's statement of work is the AME program's own work, not a commodity buy: SRI International is contracted "to maintain, enhance, and demonstrate advanced microcircuit emulation technology capability and to continue with basic technology and production development" — i.e. sustaining and advancing the emulation capability itself, which is what PE 0603680S (DLA Manufacturing Technology Program) funds; the PE's own narrative names AME among the efforts it owns (doc 105). The basis is llm-alias rather than exact-name because the announcement spells the program name out without the parenthetical acronym the index row carries, so the deterministic n-gram pass did not fire and the citation card must not claim the announcement named the program as written. §3 does not reject it: AME is a technology program, not a platform the contract merely supports; the work is specifically named, not engineering/logistics support or an unnamed IDIQ ceiling; the name is not a weak English word; "Manufacturing Technology Program" is not a CATCHALL_TITLE; and the code is not 20/30/500. No other row in the DLA index owns this name. One doubt I flag rather than hide, and it is squarely lens A's question: the appropriation line reads "fiscal 2015 direct site funds" and the contracting activity is DLA Land and Maritime, so the money colour is not stated as the RDT&E appropriation that 0603680S sits in — if that funding reads as DLA operating/working-capital money rather than the ManTech RDT&E line, this is the money-colour failure mode and should be refuted.

refute_a.reason: Money colour fails: the announcement's own appropriation is "fiscal 2015 direct site funds" — a phrase that occurs exactly once in the whole 23,824-record queue and is not the RDT&E,DW appropriation PE 0603680S sits in (the one genuinely RDT&E record in this chunk says "research, development, test and evaluation funds" outright, and every other DLA record here is working-capital/customer money); the sole-source requirements-type maximum-ceiling vehicle out of the SPE7MX (Land and Maritime) commodity office with Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps as using customers is the DLA supply-chain production/ordering function rather than the ManTech RDT&E line's own work, so under default-to-refuted this is the customer-funded-sustainment-attached-to-an-RDT&E-line failure mode, notwithstanding that the AME mission match and the lexicon row themselves are sound.

refute_b.reason: No alternative owner exists: "Advanced Microcircuit Emulation (AME)" appears under exactly one pe_bli (0603680S) in the whole 10,464-row lexicon, and every narrative body in the loaded corpus containing "microcircuit emulation" is a 0603680S narrative (docs 216, 270, 281, 291, 301, 311, 319, 105, 182, 68) — DMEA's microelectronics line 0603720S never says emulation or microcircuit in any of its 45 narratives, so the announcement's words cannot link it equally well; the alias is real, not invented (the announcement literally reads "advanced microcircuit emulation technology capability", the index name minus its parenthetical acronym, and the row carries no weak_name flag); the evidence is the statement of work, not the contractor name; and the one era/variant alternative — the FY2017 DLA book (doc 216, the book closest to this FY2015 award) calls the same microcircuit-emulation line of effort "Material Acquisition Electronics" — is itself an index row carrying the SAME pe_bli 0603680S, so the PE-level attribution is identical under either name. Lens P's "fiscal 2015 direct site funds" money-colour doubt is real but is lens A's question, not mine, and I leave it to that lens.
